definition: The rechargeable power cell in laptops and phones; it wears out after many charge cycles and can swell when it fails.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A small video camera, usually in the display bezel above the screen and often paired with a microphone, used for video calls.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

definition: The wires that carry wireless signals to the laptop's network card, usually routed through the hinge into the display lid for better reception.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

definition: The touch-sensitive layer of a touchscreen that turns finger or pen contact into input the device can read.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: The general category of sign-in methods that identify a person by a unique body trait, such as a fingerprint, face, voice, or retina.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A sensor, often on the keyboard or power button, that reads the ridges of a finger to unlock the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A camera-based unlock method that compares the user's face with a stored image to verify identity.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A reader built into a laptop or phone that exchanges data with cards, tags, or payment terminals held within a few centimeters.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A filter over a display that narrows the viewing angle so only the person directly in front can read the screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A steel cable wrapped around a fixed object and locked into a slot on a laptop so it cannot be carried away.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

definition: A pen-shaped tool used to write, draw, or tap on a touchscreen more precisely than a finger.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A flat surface that accepts pen input and sends it to the computer, used with illustration and note-taking programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A flat, touch-sensitive surface that moves the cursor as a finger slides across it, built into laptops or added over USB or wireless.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A small pressure-sensitive nub between the G, H, and B keys that moves the cursor like a tiny joystick.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: Headphones combined with a microphone, connected by cable or wirelessly, for calls and online meetings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A base that a laptop connects to so it works like a desktop, keeping the monitor, keyboard, network, and charger attached.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A simple add-on that only gives a laptop extra ports, without the charging and expansion features of a full desktop base.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: Apple's proprietary eight-pin reversible connector for charging and data on older iPhones and iPads.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A small, non-reversible USB connector that was standard on Android phones for years and is now mostly replaced by USB-C.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: An older and thicker small USB connector, found on early phones, cameras, and some accessories, and rarely seen today.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: Sharing a phone's cellular internet connection with one computer, usually over a USB cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A phone feature that shares its cellular internet connection by creating a small Wi-Fi network that other devices join.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: Very short-range wireless technology, about 4 cm, used for contactless payments and for tapping two devices together to share data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: A short-range wireless standard, usually up to about 10 meters, that connects headsets, speakers, keyboards, and wearables to a device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 2: Mobile Device Accessories and Connectivity Options

definition: The step that connects two short-range wireless devices so they trust each other, sometimes by entering a PIN.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: A setting that switches off a device's radios, including cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth, with one control.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: A small removable card that stores a subscriber's account details so a phone can connect to a carrier's network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: A satellite navigation system that gives a receiver its position anywhere on Earth; it does nothing if the device's location setting is off.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: Finding a phone's position by measuring its signals to several cell towers, which works without a view of satellites.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: The device setting that lets apps use the device's position from satellites, cell towers, or Wi-Fi; turning it off blocks maps and tracking.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: Using a device's position to trigger an action, such as an alert or a policy change, when it enters or leaves a defined area.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: A limit in a cellular or internet plan on how much data can be transferred each month before extra charges or slowdowns.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

definition: Central software that lets administrators enroll, configure, update, secure, and wipe an organization's phones and tablets.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: Central control of only an organization's apps on a device: installing, updating, securing, and removing them without managing the whole device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: A policy that lets employees use their personal phones and laptops for work under the organization's rules.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: A policy where the organization buys and controls the device but lets the employee also use it for personal tasks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: Keeping mail, contacts, calendars, and files the same on a phone, a computer, and the cloud by copying changes between them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

definition: An online service, such as OneDrive or iCloud, that keeps files on remote servers so they can be reached from any device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support
